title: Session history: a changing navigable continuation activates a target entry that a queue-jumping synchronous navigation has replaced or removed

labels.name: compat
labels.description: Standard is not web compatible or proprietary feature needs standardizing

body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard?

[Apply the history step](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/browsing-the-web.html#apply-the-history-step) retains each changing navigable’s target entry early — in the per-navigable job (_“Let *targetEntry* be *navigable*’s current session history entry.”_), which stores it in a [changing navigable continuation state](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/browsing-the-web.html#changing-navigable-continuation-state). The run then waits for those jobs in its _“While *completedChangeJobs* does not equal *totalChangeJobs*”_ loop. And while it waits, synchronous navigation steps jump the queue, by design. Each of those runs [finalize a same-document navigation](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/browsing-the-web.html#finalize-a-same-document-navigation) — which edits the very entry list that the retained entry came from: It either replaces an entry in its slot (_“Replace *entryToReplace* with *targetEntry* in *targetEntries*.”_), or removes entries (_“Clear the forward session history of *traversable*.”_).

**Nothing looks at the retained entry again.** When the continuation is dequeued, the run reads _“Let *targetEntry* be *changingNavigableContinuation*’s target entry.”_, and goes on to _“activate history entry *targetEntry* for *navigable*”_ — even if that entry is no longer among the navigable’s session history entries. But everything around it is computed from the list as it is *then*: _“Let *entriesForNavigationAPI* be the result of getting session history entries for the navigation API given *navigable* and *targetStep*.”_ So, the entry that gets activated and the state derived for it can disagree.

The window for that is the job’s fetch: The synchronous navigation has to land after the job has retained its target, and before the continuation is dequeued — so, while _“attempt to populate the history entry’s document”_ is still waiting on the network, with the old document still active and still running script. Two cases:

#### 1. `location.reload()`, then `history.replaceState()` during the reload’s fetch

```js
location.reload();
// Later, while the response is still in flight:
history.replaceState({ replaced: true }, "", "?replaced");
```

1. [Reload](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/browsing-the-web.html#reload) sets reload pending on the active entry E’s document state, and appends its traversal steps. The reload’s run retains E as the navigable’s target entry, starts repopulating E’s document, and waits.
2. The [URL and history update steps](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/browsing-the-web.html#url-and-history-update-steps) synchronously create a new entry E2 (with E’s document state), make E2 the active entry, and append their synchronous navigation steps. Those jump the queue — and finalize a same-document navigation replaces E with E2 in the entry list. E is no longer in the session history.
3. The response arrives, and the continuation is dequeued — with E. *entriesForNavigationAPI* is computed from the list, so it holds E2 and not E. E gets activated anyway. And [update document for history step application](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/browsing-the-web.html#update-document-for-history-step-application) then runs _“Initialize the navigation API entries for a new document given *navigation*, *entriesForNavigationAPI*, and *entry*.”_ — whose last step, _“Set *navigation*’s current entry index to the result of getting the navigation API entry index of *initialSHE* within *navigation*.”_, comes out as −1, since no `NavigationHistoryEntry` in the entry list has E as its session history entry.

So per spec, the reloaded document starts out with `navigation.currentEntry` null, with a `navigation.entries()` that doesn’t hold its own entry, and in a navigable whose active session history entry isn’t among its session history entries. After that, the document’s own `replaceState()` calls can’t land either: They reach _“Replace *entryToReplace* with *targetEntry* in *targetEntries*.”_ with an *entryToReplace* (E) that isn’t in *targetEntries*.

#### 2. `history.forward()`, then `history.pushState()` during the traversal’s fetch

```js
// From a document that has forward history:
history.forward();
// Later, while the response is still in flight:
history.pushState(null, "", "#pushed");
```

1. The traversal’s run retains T — the entry one step forward — starts populating T’s document, and waits.
2. The `pushState()` steps jump the queue. The traversable’s current session history step is still the pre-traversal one — since the run only sets it in its second-to-last step. So, finalize a same-document navigation’s _“Clear the forward session history of *traversable*.”_ removes T (_“Remove every session history entry from *entryList* that has a step greater than *step*.”_), and then appends the pushed entry P at _“*traversable*’s current session history step + 1”_ — which is the step T had.
3. The response arrives, and the continuation is dequeued — with T. T gets activated, though it’s been cleared away. *entriesForNavigationAPI* holds P rather than T, so the new document’s current entry index comes out as −1 again. And the run ends with _“Set *traversable*’s current session history step to *targetStep*.”_ — a step which P now holds. So, the navigable’s active entry (T) and the entry at the traversable’s current step (P) are different entries, with different documents.

If the synchronous navigation’s steps get to run *before* the job has retained its target (with both calls in one task, e.g.), then none of that happens: The nested run points the navigable’s current session history entry at E2 or P first, and the job retains that entry instead.

#### Related

A navigation’s own just-appended entry can get cleared the same way — by a `pushState()` from the document that’s being navigated away from. Item 2 of #12576 covers that, along with the step bookkeeping around it. This issue is about the other half: what a continuation does with a target entry that’s been replaced or removed in the meantime.

The job’s own asserts are exposed to the same race. For “push”, e.g., the first half of _“Assert: *targetEntry*’s step is *displayedEntry*’s step + 1 and *targetEntry*’s document state’s ever populated is false.”_ doesn’t hold once *displayedEntry* is the entry from a jumped `pushState()` — which takes that same step.

### Implementations

As far as I can tell, no engine holds on to a pre-resolved target entry like that. Each one settles a load’s entry against the list as it is when the load commits — so, the committed document’s entry is always in the session history.

- **Traversals.** The target gets resolved when the traversal actually runs — and if it’s gone by then, there’s no traversal. WebKit’s `ScheduledHistoryNavigation::fire` returns early unless the back/forward list still `containsItem` the target. Gecko’s `CanonicalBrowsingContext::HistoryGo` (reached from `ChildSHistory::Go`) computes the target index from the then-current index, and bails if it’s out of range. Blink’s `NavigationControllerImpl::GoToOffsetFromRenderer` checks `CanGoToOffset` when the request arrives. And if a push prunes the target while the traversal’s load is in flight, then Blink’s push commit (`NavigationControllerImpl::InsertOrReplaceEntry`) discards the pending entry along with the pruned ones. Should that load still commit, `NavigationControllerImpl::ClassifyNavigation` finds no existing entry for it, and treats it as a new one (“resurrect that entry”) — added after the pushed entry.
- **Navigations.** A `pushState()` leaves a pending cross-document load alone (Gecko `nsDocShell::UpdateURLAndHistory`, WebKit `FrameLoader::updateURLAndHistory`, Blink `RenderFrameHostImpl::DidCommitSameDocumentNavigation`). And the load’s entry gets added when the load commits — after the pushed entries: Gecko `CanonicalBrowsingContext::SessionHistoryCommit`, WebKit `HistoryController::updateForStandardLoad`, Blink `NavigationControllerImpl::RendererDidNavigateToNewEntry`.
- **Reload plus `replaceState()`.** The engines do differ on whose URL and state win: In my testing, Firefox keeps the `replaceState()` URL and state on the entry (with the reloaded document being the one fetched from the original URL) — while Chrome’s reload commit overwrites them. But in neither one does the reloaded document end up with an entry that’s not in the session history.

Ladybird implements the spec’s queue model as written, and crashed on case 1 in the wild — with a current entry index of −1. https://github.com/LadybirdBrowser/ladybird/pull/12084 makes it look up the target again when the continuation runs, as in the first fix below.

### Imaginable fixes

- When a continuation is dequeued, look up its target entry again (by getting the target history entry given *navigable* and *targetStep*, e.g.) — rather than trusting the retained one. Then: If the slot holds a same-document replacement of the retained entry (an entry with the same document state, at the same step), activate the replacement instead — or otherwise define which of the two entries’ URL and state win. If a traversal’s target is gone, either finish the job without activating anything, or add the entry again after the pushed ones, as Blink does. And if a navigation’s own new entry is gone, add it again after the pushed entries (which is what all three engines amount to) — or settle it however #12576 gets settled;
- make the continuation’s target a slot (the navigable plus a step) rather than an entry, and have finalize a same-document navigation and clear the forward session history keep the in-flight runs’ slots valid — or cancel the runs whose slots they remove; or
- stop synchronous navigations from jumping the queue once a run has retained its targets, for the navigables whose targets it has retained — though that gives up what the jump exists for: getting the synchronous navigation’s entry into place before its document unloads.
